function: Robust over-the-air gradient aggregation (AirComp) for federated learning against interference, by setting passive RIS phase shifts and device transmit power in closed form (pp. 5-6).
system: Single-antenna PS and K=20 devices (scalar cascaded channel, p. 3); passive reflecting RIS, N=256 elements; M=10 interferers; B=1 MHz; carrier frequency not stated (pp. 8-9).
method: Closed-form RIS phase/power design (non-learned); learned element is an MLP (MNIST) and CNN (CIFAR-10) trained by federated SGD over AirComp, non-IID data (p. 8).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rayleigh small-scale fading CN(0,I_N), path-loss exponent 2.2, PS-RIS 200 m, devices in 300 m disk (pp. 3, 8); MNIST and CIFAR-10 for the FL task.
test_conditions: Each FL run trained and tested in one simulated setting; sweeps over N, P, K, M and RIS phase noise; no unseen channel or scenario (pp. 8-10).
baselines: Non-learned: BEV+RandPhase (random RIS), BEV+RR (round-robin RIS), BEV-minMSE (optimized RIS phases, like [54]); earlier aggregation designs: BEV [23], random orthogonalization BEV-RO with multi-antenna PS [50] (pp. 8-9).
metrics: Normalized MSE of gradient estimation (analytical vs Monte-Carlo); test accuracy versus communication rounds on MNIST and CIFAR-10; convergence-rate bound (pp. 8-10).
q1_support: p. 3: "denote the small-scale fading channel" with hp, hr,i ~ CN(0, IN); p. 8: "The path loss exponent for all the links is 2.2." Custom Rayleigh simulator; no 3GPP model or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 9: "testing accuracy on the MNIST datasets for transmission powers of 0 and 15 dBm" is a power sweep with separate runs; no model trained in one setting is tested in another.
q3_support: p. 8: "the RIS phases are randomly selected" (non-learned baseline BEV+RandPhase); p. 9: "multi-antenna receiver at the PS in [50] is adopted for model aggregation and interference suppression" (earlier published design), compared on MSE (Figs. 3-6) and test accuracy (Figs. 8-9).
q4_support: p. 8: "a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) with D = 23860 parameters is trained via" the AirFL is only the size of the trained FL model; no complexity, operation count or runtime of the RIS/power design is reported.
q5_support: p. 8: "image classification on the two popular datasets", MNIST and CIFAR-10, are learning-task datasets only; channels are simulated and no code or data link is given.
notes: Closed-form RIS phase and power design for AirComp FL (no trained physical-layer model). Included only through the FL-over-the-air rule: the learned element is the MLP/CNN trained across devices; area 7 because the problem is the over-the-air aggregation itself (pp. 5-6). q3 = 1 rests on the FL-OTA reading: BEV [23] and random orthogonalization [50] are earlier published aggregation designs, and random-phase RIS is a simple non-learned baseline; reviewer to confirm. Single-antenna PS and devices are inferred from the scalar cascaded channel h_i^E (p. 3), not stated in words.
